title: A fixed background fraction gives no stable prediction gain for KIC 8164262 aperture amplitudes in Kepler Q2 to Q16
abstract: We test a background error model for small changes in the known strong oscillation of KIC 8164262. A constant fractional error in the reported aperture background implies a linear relation between measured amplitude and background divided by aperture flux. In 15 Kepler release 25 quarters, the model gives held-group mean squared error of 234.82 ppm squared against 247.18 for constant amplitude with a cubic baseline. A wider orbital mask gives 192.02 against 194.22. A quadratic baseline gives 194.28 against 186.88, which reverses the gain. Corrected flux gives more stable gains over a constant but a season model predicts better in all three choices. This result limits one simple background model; it does not exclude other background or detector effects. The two flux products share exposures. There is no independent telescope confirmation or new planet claim. Code, source hashes, quarter measurements, background metadata, held-group predictions, and figures support reproduction. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-4aeaf50023ea; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
